sources.title: Jacques Leider: Présentation et commentaire (1999)
sources.note: Original printed125 directly checked: December1784 resistance collapsed, January1785 capital capture. Reused Mrauk U packet source, which already attributes122 words. Combined budget explicitly checked.

sources.title: Arthur Phayre: History of Burma, chapter XX (1883)
sources.note: Original colonial-era history transcribed by Vajirayana digital library, printed214 to 223. Royal household/captives and Mahamuni image removal; later revolt and cross-border flight. Its precise December capital-entry date differs from Leider; use Leider for exact conquest chronology. Colonial judgments not adopted.

sources.title: Treaty of Yandabo, 24 February 1826, English text
sources.note: Full primary treaty transcription directly read, article3 specifically cedes Arakan, Ramree, Cheduba, Sandoway and uses mountains as boundary. Article2 does not simply cede all listed northeast Indian territories; no such generalization made.

sources.title: Alleyne Ireland: The Province of Burma, volume I (1907)
sources.note: Library of Congress original scan indexed directly; organization section reproduces resolution31 January1862 and minute10 February1862, Arakan/Pegu/Tenasserim divisions and later administrative continuity. Direct fetch failed, full original indexed excerpt checked. University of Chicago commissioned report; colonial evaluative claims not adopted.

sources.title: Francis Buchanan in Southeast Bengal (1798), edited by Willem van Schendel (1992), excerpt
sources.note: Original scholarly edition excerpt, printed60 to 61, April1798 Ramu and refugee Rakain testimony. Exact local gardens described outside Arakan, explicitly a cross-border family comparison. Historical slurs and author ethnic rankings not adopted. Original indexed extract supplies full text; direct PDF has no OCR.

sources.title: W. F. Nuthall: Memorandum on the trade of Arakan and Akyab (1849), edited by Michael Charney
sources.note: SOAS Bulletin of Burma Research1.1(2003), document4, printed69 to 73; originally Straits Times and Singapore Journal of Commerce4 December1849 pp4 to 5. University metadata checked; full author-uploaded ResearchGate mirror read. All mirrors and reprints pooled as one work. Only1849 document used, not1777 account.

sources.title: Akyab District: historical gazetteer extract, Anglo-Burmese Library
sources.note: Full seven-page extract directly read; colonial late1870s description, especially PDF3 to 5 administration, prison, hospital, school. Reproduces British Burma Gazetteer-era reports; provenance is a modern transcription, not an inspected original manuscript. Obvious garbled population sentence on PDF2 not used. All extract passages pooled below200 words.

sources.title: Emanuel Forchhammer: Report on the Antiquities of Arakan (1891/1892), Akyab
sources.note: SOAS original scan indexed printed60 to 61. Direct fetch failed. Original targeted search verified1876 Davies report,1834 custody orders,1849 Mah Ming Oung construction/tank and family custodians. Same passage independently present in Richard Temple1926 Indian Antiquary55 pp28 to 29, but not counted as a second source. Foundation dates conflict and are not asserted.

sources.title: Francis Buchanan: A Comparative Vocabulary of Some of the Languages Spoken in the Burma Empire (1799; scholarly reprint 2003)
sources.note: SOAS Bulletin of Burma Research1.1 printed55, exact table and introduction, original Asiatic Researches5 pp237 to 238. University original indexed full text directly verified, direct fetch failed. Original1799 scan also checked via indexed text. Roman spellings Bel/Tara/Pannæ are collector transcription, not native manuscript or standard modern orthography.

sources.title: J. S. Furnivall: Colonial Policy and Practice (1948), Economic Progress
sources.note: University-hosted original scan indexed printed95: early1870s Akyab millers, advances, shipping shortages and broken buyers cartel. Used localized example rather than generalized claim of prosperity or unanimous peasant independence. Underlying cited trade reports1868 to 1876.

batchIdentityNotes.identity: Exact indexed1783 to 1878 regional record, no aliases. All ancient and Mrauk U IDs remain separately covered or unclaimed. It cannot be called one independent state for the full period.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Identical decoded outline for1783 to 1800,1800 to 1815 and1815 to 1878; bbox92.123121E,17.642437N,95.363154E,22.202652N. It matches late Mrauk U outline, hiding1784/85 and1826 sovereignty changes. Public warning; no repaired boundary invented.
batchIdentityNotes.dateScope: Historical phases1783 to 1785,1785 to 1826,1826 to 1862,1862 to 1878. Later gazetteer/survey accounts explicitly retrospective sources for dated events or near-endpoint conditions. Ramu household scene is outside Arakan in refugee borderland, visibly so.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Buchanan1799 printed238/SOAS2003 printed55 provides exact Latin-letter transcription and glosses. No native-script facsimile claimed. Community label is reported historical usage, not a modern citizenship argument.
batchIdentityNotes.budget: Leider1999 reused Mrauk U source; earlier packet122 words included in combined-work check. Other distinct works and mirrors pooled. National Army Museum source avoided because existing Burma card already uses most of its allowance.
